service.description: Next.js's own credential: `python scripts/service_token.py` prints one (five minutes).
service.name: X-Vertex-Service

session.description: A signed-in user's session: the website's auth_token cookie.

post.description:
The same answer whether or not the address has an account; an email
only for an account that can sign in with a password.

A screened candidate creates their account from the invite. Name,
email, phone and country come from the candidate record, never the
request.

Sets a new password from the emailed link. Every session of the
account ends (the token_version trigger).

A staff or partner account, created by an admin or director, sets its
first password from the setup link. The link works until a password is
set.

POST /api/applications: the Candidate Information Form, the first
thing anyone fills in. A new candidate starts at "identified"; only a
Regional Recruiter entering a walk-in lead becomes its recruiter, and a
self-applicant goes to HR. A self-applicant is screened at once, and
invited to create an account if they pass.

put.description:
PUT /api/applications/[id]: the legacy hiring status and the internal
notes (edited from a case). A case opens from the candidate's own
lifecycle status, not from this. The candidate hears about a status
change, not a notes edit.

post.description:
Sign-in only: an account must already exist. A linked account is found
by Google's own id; linking by email needs Google to have verified the
address, never re-links an account linked to another Google account, and
drops a password nobody proved they own (#131's rules).

verifyPasswordLogin() and startSession(): the same checks, messages
and status codes. The website records and answers a per-address
refusal itself; this one is per account.

Ends the session server-side, not just its cookies: the refresh token
names it even when the access token has expired; without one, the
signed-in user's own session. Always answers the same way.

refreshSession(): rotation, the race window, and reuse detection. The
refusal's reason goes back in details: on "superseded" the website keeps
the cookies the winning request set; on "reused" it raises the alert.

get.description: The caller's live sessions, for the "Active sessions" panel.

delete.description: Scoped to the caller: another user's session id matches nothing (404).

get.description:
Newest first. ?scope=mine keeps the campaigns with a target for the
caller's own country, its region, or the whole campaign: the reporting
cycle's "Campaign" picker (Supervisory Reporting Framework §3.1).

delete.description: Its targets, and the recruiter allocations drawn from them, go with it.

post.description:
Cascades a numeric target to a country, a region, or the whole
campaign (FR-3.3).

Registration (POST /api/auth/register) links the account it has just
created to the candidate the screening invite was for. Users stay with
the website until they move (data-ownership.md §2.3), so the website
creates the User and only Next.js itself may call this. FastAPI checks
the invite for itself, and that the account is that candidate's.

Claiming the invite is what "guided to apply" means now. A candidate
who attached every required document on the form is submitted at once,
since no upload will come along to do it.

put.description: PUT /api/candidates/profile: a signed-in candidate edits Section 2.

delete.description:
DELETE /api/candidates/[id]: removes a submission that shouldn't be
there, with its applications, documents and messages. Refused once a
case exists, whatever its status: a case is a permanent record.

patch.description: PATCH /api/candidates/[id]: progressive detail edits and consent.

PATCH /api/candidates/[id]/application: staff correcting the
programme, travel and visa answers on the candidate's latest
application, and on a partner submission's own copy of them.

post.description: POST /api/candidates/[id]/messages.

patch.description: PATCH /api/candidates/[id]/messages/[messageId].

PATCH /api/candidates/[id]/status: a role-gated lifecycle move
(SRS FR-2.4), the screening gate on "screened" (FR-2.5) and the
supervisor's return for correction (FR-2.7).

post.description:
POST /api/cases/[id]/contract: Operations issue the contract, sent
for the candidate to sign in the portal.

POST /api/cases/[id]/contract/sign: a simple electronic signature
(typed legal name, the signed-in session, time and address). Only the
candidate the contract is for can sign; staff never sign for them.

patch.description:
PATCH /api/cases/[id]/ops-review: confirms or flags the paperwork
before the operational process begins. It can be changed later; it
never opens or closes a case.

PATCH /api/cases/[id]/overturn: clears a rejection. Reopening it puts
the candidate and application back to "approved", where opening the
case left them.

post.description:
POST /api/cases/[id]/payments: Finance records a collected milestone
payment, with a receipt reference or file (SRS FR-4.5).

POST /api/cases/[id]/payments/invoice, once the website has sent the
email: a pending payment for the invoiced stage.

The invoice's checks, writing nothing: what the website needs to send
the email before /invoice records it.

POST /api/cases/[id]/payments/link: a Stripe Payment Link for one
stage, on the stage's provisioned Price, for a self-applicant's case.
Pending until the webhook (or check-status) sees it paid.

delete.description:
DELETE /api/cases/[id]/payments/[paymentId]: Finance removes a
payment recorded in error, in either status. Nothing references a
CasePayment; its receipt file is kept.

post.description:
POST /api/cases/[id]/payments/[paymentId]/check-status: asks Stripe
whether the payment's link has been paid, for when the webhook never
came, and collects it if so.

POST /api/cases/[id]/payments/[paymentId]/mark-paid: Finance confirms
a pending payment arrived (a bank transfer, say), with the uploaded
receipt as the proof, so a receipt is required.

patch.description:
PATCH /api/cases/[id]/payments/[paymentId]/receipt: attaches, swaps
or (with null) removes a payment's invoice or receipt file, in either
status.

PATCH /api/cases/[id]/reject: closes the case for good, and the
candidate and application with it. HR and the partner are told.

post.description:
POST /api/cases/[id]/remind: Operations chasing a delayed document or
payment, by email to the candidate or their partner.

patch.description: PATCH /api/cases/[id]/retention: the 90-day follow-up is done.

PATCH /api/cases/[id]/stage (SRS FR-4.2): closes the open stage and
opens the next, earns a referral commission at its milestones, and
starts the 90-day retention follow-up at the last stage (FR-4.7).

get.description: Every country with its region, by name.

delete.description:
Candidates, cases, staff assignments and the rest let go of the
country (SET NULL or CASCADE); anything that still requires it makes
Postgres refuse, which is a 409.

patch.description: Renames a country and/or moves it to another region.

get.description:
The documents this destination requires beyond the universal set
(passport, photo, CV): the form's "Required for: X". An unknown country
has none.

put.description: Replaces the country's whole list (the admin ticks a checklist).

post.description: A new type from just a label; its key is the label, slugified.

delete.description:
Refused while an uploaded document uses the type. Countries that
required it stop requiring it, each removal on the audit trail.

post.description:
POST /api/upload?type=<key>[&candidate_id=|&partner_candidate_id=],
multipart: file, and label for type "other".

POST /api/upload with X-Upload-Token: a self-applicant attaching
documents to the form they have just submitted, before any account
exists. Only Next.js may call this; the token decides the candidate.

assertDocumentReadable: Next.js asks before a stored file leaves the
server (a download, an email attachment), for a user or for itself.
Uploads are scanned before storage; this catches those accepted while
the scanner was unreachable, scanning them now. Infected is always
refused; unscanned and still unreachable is served (fail-open).

patch.description:
PATCH /api/documents/[id]/verify (SRS FR-2.7). Rejecting a partner
submission's document doesn't touch the submission's status: the partner
replaces the file.

put.description: Creates or replaces the override for body.event.

get.description: Every client, by name, with how many jobs each has.
One client, with its linked jobs, newest first.

post.description:
POST /api/exceptions: any staff role, at any time, independent of
the reporting cadence. It starts at the raiser's tier.

patch.description:
PATCH /api/exceptions/[id]: push it up a tier, or decide it. A
decision of "escalated" also goes up a tier and stays open; any other
closes it.

get.description: Every policy, the most recently changed first.

post.description: Creates or replaces the policy for body.country_id (null = global).

delete.description:
Its stages go with it; applications and payments for it are removed
by Postgres (CASCADE). A job a partner submission or a recorded payment
still points to is a 409.

post.description: Attaches one of the canonical sectors to a programme.

delete.description: Its positions go with it; applications that picked one let go of it.

post.description: e.g. "Grape Picker" under Italy's Agriculture sector.

patch.description: A position's title and city; a null city clears it.

post.description:
The manual retry for a sync that failed (e.g. Stripe was down):
runs now and reports the outcome.

get.description: The signed-in caller, from the database (as Next.js's /api/auth/me).

delete.description:
DELETE /api/partner-candidates/[id]: an erroneous or duplicate
submission, with its candidate (and their applications, documents and
messages). Refused once a case exists.

patch.description:
PATCH /api/partner-candidates/[id]/create-case: HR approves the
submission and opens its case. The partner already screened the
candidate, so they go straight to "approved".

PATCH /api/partner-candidates/[id]/overturn: a rejection undone, the
submission back to "submitted", where it was when it was rejected.

The linked candidate keeps its status: rejecting never changed it, so
undoing the rejection leaves it as it was. (Until 2026-10-30 this set
the candidate to "approved", as the website did, though no case
existed; the owner decided an overturn reinstates the previous status.)

PATCH /api/partner-candidates/[id]/reject: sent back to the partner
to correct; not a dead end.

post.description: POST /api/partner/candidates: a fresh submission.

POST /api/partner/candidates/draft: work in progress, any fields; no
checks until it's submitted.

delete.description:
DELETE /api/partner/candidates/[id]: a partner abandoning its own
unfinished draft, with the files it uploaded. A real submission is
never self-deleted, only rejected.

patch.description:
PATCH /api/partner/candidates/[id]: a partner correcting its own
submission, or staff re-saving a draft they're entering. A bridged
submission's candidate and latest application follow.

post.description:
POST /api/partner/candidates/[id]/submit: a draft finished, upgraded in
place, against the same bar as a fresh submission.
A PayPal order for the signed-in user's application fee.

Captures the user's approved order, once PayPal confirms it's theirs
for this job's fee, and records the payment.
Stripe's event, passed on by the website as it came.

get.description:
A recruiter's notes, newest first: a recruiter reads their own (the
id defaults to, and must be, theirs), a Country Supervisor any one of
their recruiters', admin anyone's.

post.description: A Country Supervisor's note to one of their own recruiters.

get.description:
A recruiter sees their own allocations, a Country Supervisor their
recruiters', everyone else all of them. Most recently set first.

post.description: Sets one recruiter's share of a campaign target (creates or replaces it).

One rule per (country, milestone): the existing one is updated. A
rule saved by a concurrent request is updated on a second try.

pending -> approved. A zero commission is settled as paid when it's
earned, so only a payable amount gets here.
approved -> paid; the reference and method are optional.

get.description: Every region with its countries, both by name.

post.description:
Submits a report at the caller's own scope, consolidating the given
verified child reports into it.

patch.description:
Only the original submitter (or admin) corrects and resubmits a
returned report. The content is checked after the report, as the
website did.
Sends an incomplete or incorrect report back to its submitter.

The controlling position accepts the report as submitted: a Country
Supervisor or In-House Supervisor "verifies", the director "approves"
a portfolio report (§8.2). The parent report isn't created here: its
submitter reviews the roll-up and submits it themselves.

delete.description: Applications that chose the sector let go of it (SET NULL).

get.description: Every setting, as a key-value map.

put.description: Sets the keys present in the body, in one transaction.

post.description:
Sets one KPI-row target for a direct report, keyed to a label their
own report's KPI table uses for that cycle (creates or replaces it).

Creates the month's draft scorecard for a direct report, or updates
it: each area sent sets the rating and evidence it carries; areas not
sent keep theirs.

patch.description:
Computes the weighted overall score from the rated areas, derives the
performance category and required action, and locks the scorecard. Only
its author (or admin) finalizes it, and only once every area is rated.

post.description:
A new staff account with no password: the setup email lets them set
their own.

delete.description:
Removes an account; its dependants follow the foreign keys, as with
Prisma. Nobody removes themselves, or the last admin.

patch.description:
Role, supervisor and countries (SRS FR-1.1, FR-1.3, FR-1.4). A field
left out is left alone; assigned_country_ids replaces the whole list.

post.description:
A temporary password, shown to the admin once and never stored or
logged in plain text. The user's sessions end (token_version trigger).

delete.description:
For offboarding without deleting the account, or a suspected
compromise: the user's next request is refused.
